name: Vegetarian Fesenjan
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss aubergine cubes with 30 ml oil and 4 g salt; spread in one layer and roast 25–30 minutes until browned and tender. Grind walnuts finely, stopping before they become butter.
Meanwhile heat remaining oil in a heavy pan and cook onion 8 minutes until golden. Stir in cinnamon and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add ground walnuts and stir over low heat for 3 minutes, then pour in vegetable stock gradually while whisking. Simmer very gently 20 minutes, stirring often so the walnuts do not stick.
Stir in pomegranate molasses, brown sugar, remaining salt and black pepper. Simmer another 10 minutes until the sauce turns dark and thick; balance sourness with a little more sugar only if needed.
Fold roasted aubergine into the walnut sauce and warm 5 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, scatter pomegranate arils on top and serve with saffron rice.
tips: Keep the walnut sauce at a gentle simmer; a hard boil can scorch the nuts. Fesenjan is intentionally dark and sweet-sour from walnuts and pomegranate.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
